steps.title: Add a server with fixed fields
steps.body: In Servers, open the connection card for an MCP server. Enter the endpoint and any authentication value the server owner supplied; MCP Core does not invent supported servers. Save the entry, then confirm it appears in the list. Take the endpoint and credential from the addon that owns the server, not from a chat message.

steps.title: Diagnose an unreachable server
steps.body: If a saved server reports unreachable, check that its process is actually running and that the endpoint exactly matches what the owning addon displays. A wrong port is a common cause. Correct the endpoint before retrying the connection; re-saving unchanged details does not help.

learning_outcomes: Know that requests are not approval

steps.title: Grant addon access explicitly
steps.body: Permissions lists which addons may use a server. Select the addon, such as Companion Chess, and choose to allow it; requests from the addon appear here for your decision. Approval is manual by design. Only grant access to addons you are actively using, and remove grants when you stop using a server.

steps.title: Know that requests are not approval
steps.body: An addon's Request access only queues a permission; you approve it on this tab. A connected server without a permission grant will not let the addon act. Connection and permission are two gates. Removing a grant stops future calls without deleting the connection.

steps.title: Review the tools a server exposes
steps.body: Tools lists the tool names and descriptions offered by a connected server. Read them before granting any addon access so you know what could be invoked. Tool descriptions come from the server, not from NC, so treat them as reference. Availability here does not imply any tool runs automatically.
steps.target_hint: This control may depend on available content or a loaded addon. Read the step here; no service or provider is enabled by the guide.

steps.title: Match tools to the addon’s needs
steps.body: Pair a tool you recognise with the addon that owns it, such as chess moves with Companion Chess. If a tool is missing, reconnect the server and refresh before assuming a permission problem. Missing tools and missing permissions look similar but need different fixes.
